descriptionChirho: To invoke evil or divine judgment upon someone, to pronounce a curse. Used in all its inflectional forms (present participle, aorist indicative, present indicative, present imperative, perfect participle) with a single consistent meaning throughout the NT. Occurs in Jesus' teaching to bless those who curse you (Matt 5:44; Luke 6:28), Jesus cursing the fig tree (Mark 11:21), Paul's exhortation to bless and not curse (Rom 12:14), James' warning about cursing people made in God's image (Jas 3:9), and the eschatological pronouncement of the cursed being sent to eternal fire (Matt 25:41). Rendered Arabic لعن, German verfluchen, French maudire, Hebrew קִלֵּל/אָרוּר, Hindi शाप देना, Korean 저주하다, Spanish maldecir.
